themes.title: Molecular interfaces and biophysics
themes.introduction: Study of lipid membranes, their phase transitions and their interactions through molecular simulation and data analysis.

image.alt: Placeholder illustration of a molecular interface.

highlights.label: Research focus
highlights.value: Lipid membranes, phase transitions and membrane instabilities.

highlights.label: Computational approaches
highlights.value: Molecular simulation, data analysis and machine learning.

highlights.label: Publications
highlights.value: Three first-author articles dedicated to lipid membranes and MLLPA.

paragraphs: My work focuses on phase transitions, membrane instabilities and the interactions of lipid membranes with peptides or proteins.
It combines molecular dynamics simulations, classification, scientific data processing and machine-learning approaches, including three-dimensional convolutional neural networks.
This research led to the development of MLLPA, a documented and reusable Python module for machine-learning-assisted analysis of lipid membrane phases.
I continue occasional scientific collaborations related to lipid membranes and MLLPA. Work associated with a three-dimensional CNN has not yet been published.

highlights.label: Automation

highlights.label: Main publication
highlights.value: Lead author of an article on spatial light modulation for iSCAT microscopy.

paragraphs: My work in optics and photonics focuses on the design, construction and operation of instrumental platforms for observing biological and nanoscale systems.
It includes the construction and qualification of a complete interferometric scattering microscope, the design of experimental protocols, sample preparation, and data acquisition and analysis.

It also includes the development of LabVIEW software for controlling and automating scientific instruments, together with work on an automated epifluorescence microscope conducted under a confidentiality agreement.

highlights.label: Experimental infrastructure
highlights.value: Creation of a molecular communication laboratory and an operational testbed.

highlights.label: Interdisciplinary system
highlights.value: Chemistry, microfluidics, instrumentation, electronics and signal processing.

highlights.label: Publications
highlights.value: Two articles as first author and lead writer.

paragraphs: My work in molecular communication involved creating a laboratory and an experimental platform combining chemistry, microfluidics, instrumentation, electronics, signal processing and machine learning.
The testbed enabled the production, transmission and detection of molecular signals to experimentally validate chemical-reaction-based communication concepts.

I also developed a one-dimensional CNN with Python, TensorFlow and scikit-learn to analyse UV-Visible spectroscopy signals, together with six open-source syringe pumps combining mechanical design, 3D printing, Arduino, I²C communication, C++ and Python.
This work led to two publications for which I was the first author and lead writer.
